exposure: COVID-19 pandemic (first wave, March 15 to May 15, 2020)
outcome: Contraception utilization rates prior to delivery discharge
Contraception utilization rates at outpatient postpartum visits
Contraception utilization rates at 10 weeks' postpartum
cohort: The study included 495 perinatal individuals who received prenatal care and delivered at UMass Memorial Medical Center between mid-March and mid-May in both 2019 and 2020.
finding: Immediate postpartum long-acting reversible contraception use increased during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic compared to the previous year, while overall contraception use at 10 weeks' postpartum remained unchanged.
